Looking at the pieces, each has two straight sides (left and bottom) and two wavy sides (top and right). To build the square, the four used pieces must have their wavy edges match up perfectly in pairs along the interior seams.

- Pieces A and D have identical wavy edges (top and right), so they can pair with each other.
- Pieces B and E have identical wavy edges (top and right), so they can pair with each other.
- Piece C's wavy edges (its bumpy top and its S‑shaped right side) do not match the wavy edges of any other piece, so it cannot fit into the interior seams of the square.

Thus A, B, D, E assemble into the square (straight sides outside), and C is left over.

\boxed{C}
